Ryan: Stellaris POC asks for a simple handoff: two hosted API keys, rotation every 24h, and a revoke test. They want a one-page runbook we can give infra. cc @sam_se @maria_security
Sam_SE: We should issue ephemeral, scoped keys and deliver via one-time link or direct push to their vault. Recommended TTL 24h (48h with approval). CLI examples we give: `redwood keys create --type ephemeral --expires 24h --scopes generate,embed --note "stellaris-poc-dev1"` and `redwood keys revoke <key-id>`. Programmatic rotate: POST /v1/keys/:alias/rotate (requires service account token).
Maria_Security: Security notes: prefer 24h TTL, require audit export to their S3 (KMS recommended), document revocation steps and expected client caching behavior (in-flight requests may succeed briefly), and forbid embedding keys in frontend. Include incident contact security@redwood.ai.
Sam_SE: Revoke test runbook (short): 1) Provision keys and deliver. 2) Start load script. 3) At scheduled time we revoke via Console/CLI. 4) Client should observe 401s; collect timestamps. 5) We verify audit log entry and share exported path. Also advise disabling aggressive connection reuse during test.
Ops-bot: Internal doc link: https://docs.redwood.ai/keys/ephemeral (contains rotate lambda snippet, CLI, API, audit export instructions).
Ryan: I'll draft the one-page runbook and SecQ snippets and post for review. Sam, can you pre-create aliases stellaris-poc-dev1/dev2 so I can confirm names with the customer?
Sam_SE: On it. I'll also prepare one-time signed links with 15m TTL and set per-key quotas.
Maria_Security: I'll review the SecQ answers once posted and add the required POC clause: automatic rotation every 24h and immediate reporting of suspected compromise.
Ryan: Perfect, thanks all.
